Quit Claude Code mid-task, > start OpenAI Codex in the same directory, continue without > re-explaining the architecture, the failed approaches, or the open > questions. **Website: [aimemory.sh](https://aimemory.sh)** [](https://aimemory.sh) [](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/releases/latest) [](rust-toolchain.toml) [](LICENSE) ## Why ai-memory Your coding agent probably has a memory feature already. Claude Code takes its own notes, Cursor remembers some things, and every platform is adding more. They all have the same limits: the notes live on one machine, belong to one agent, and drop out of view when you switch tools or hand the work to a teammate. ai-memory removes those limits. - **It follows you across agents.** More than twenty harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Grok, Devin, Kimi, Kiro, and others) feed one shared memory. Quit Claude Code mid-task, open Codex in the same directory, and the next agent picks up a handoff that says where you left off, what failed, and what is still open. Their experience, what they care about, and how they think things should work. You might not know who those people are, but you can feel their perspective in the product. The industry often talks about software as though it comes out of a factory. You collect requirements, build features, and measure whether they work. Follow the process and you should get a good result. Now we're talking automating this whole pipeline with agents. But two teams can talk to similar customers, have access to the same technology, and make very different things. As a company at the frontier of AI adoption, Anthropic could be a leading indicator of how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy. Key findings Anthropic has been hiring for a smaller share of junior technical positions. This occurred as hours worked by AI agents relative to employees rapidly expanded. By August interactive AI agent hours outnumbered employees’ six to one. As AI agents diffused through the company, Anthropic began producing more code per person, closing more sales per rep, and processing more contracts.
